name: Poly Bright Quick Restore – Backup, Restore & Migration
author: Poly Bright Labs

sections.description:
Black Friday: 40% off Quick Restore Pro until December 4, 2026. Lifetime licence: pay once, use it forever. See the deal

Back up your whole WordPress site to one file, restore it in one click, or move it to a new host or domain without broken links. Works on shared hosting, even with a 2 MB upload limit.

See it in action:

Free features

  • Full-site backup in one file: database, media, plugins and themes.
  • One-click restore from a backup saved on your server, or from a file you upload. You confirm before anything is overwritten.
  • Chunked upload. Large backups are sent in small pieces, so a low PHP upload limit is not a problem.
  • Checked before restoring. The file, PHP and WordPress versions and free disk space are checked first; if something does not fit, the restore stops with a plain explanation and nothing is changed.
  • Move to a new domain safely. Serialization-safe URL replacement keeps page-builder content and widgets working.
  • Opens .wpress backups from All-in-One WP Migration (see below).

There is no trial period, and nothing in the free plugin expires.

Moving from All-in-One WP Migration?

Quick Restore restores .wpress files, so the backups you already have keep working, and you do not need All-in-One WP Migration installed. Go to Quick Restore > Restore and choose the file. It uploads in small pieces past your host’s upload limit, and the database, media, plugins, theme and site address are all restored. Backups made with a password are not supported; export them again with the password option off.

Limits

The free version restores backups up to 512 MB; Quick Restore Pro removes that limit. A single file larger than 200 MB is left out of a backup. WordPress Multisite is not supported.

Quick Restore Pro (optional paid add-on)

A separate add-on with a lifetime licence: pay once, use it forever, 12 months of updates included.

  • Pro: restores backups of any size.
  • Pro Plus: scheduled backups (daily, weekly, monthly or custom), keep-the-latest-N retention, an email with a secure download link after each scheduled backup, and a failure alert.
  • Max: Pro Plus with a licence for 5 sites.

See plans and prices
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from Plugins > Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open Quick Restore in the admin menu. Use Export to create a backup and Restore to restore one.
sections.faq:
How do I import a .wpress file?

Go to Quick Restore > Restore and choose your .wpress file. It is uploaded in chunks, checked, and you confirm before anything is overwritten. More: https://polybrightlabs.com/quick-restore/features/import-wpress-files/

Can the free version restore a backup larger than 512 MB?

No. The free version restores backups up to 512 MB, and Quick Restore Pro restores backups of any size. Backing up has no limit on total site size.

Will my links break if I move WordPress to a new domain?

When you restore a backup on a different domain, Quick Restore replaces the old site address with the new one in the database, including inside serialized data, so links and page-builder content keep working. Hard-coded file paths and addresses of other websites are not changed. More: https://polybrightlabs.com/quick-restore/features/restore-to-new-domain/

Does it work on shared hosting with a small upload limit?

Yes. Files are uploaded in pieces that fit inside your host’s upload limit, then joined on the server. Even a 2 MB PHP upload limit works. More: https://polybrightlabs.com/quick-restore/features/chunked-upload-large-files/

How do I restore my WordPress site from a backup?

Go to Quick Restore > Backups and click Restore next to a backup saved on your server, or go to Quick Restore > Restore and upload a .wpqr or .wpress file. The backup is validated, you confirm, and then your site is restored.

How do I clone a WordPress site to a new host?

Install WordPress and this plugin on the new host. On the old site, go to Quick Restore > Export and create a backup, then download it. On the new site, go to Quick Restore > Restore and upload it. If the domain is different, URLs are replaced automatically.

Where are my backups stored?

On your own server, in a Quick Restore folder inside wp-content. Nothing is sent to Poly Bright Labs: the free plugin makes no outbound connections and has no tracking.

Is Quick Restore Pro a subscription?

No. It is a one-time payment that includes 12 months of updates. The add-on keeps working after that; you only need to renew to receive newer versions.

Does it support WordPress Multisite?

Not yet.
sections.changelog:
3.0.4

  • Fixed: restoring All-in-One WP Migration (.wpress) backups now restores the database, plugins, theme and site address. Before, the restore reported success but the site did not change.
  • Fixed: chunked upload failed with “File too large” on hosts where memory_limit is unlimited.
  • Improved: the Restore screen says when Quick Restore Pro has removed the 512 MB limit.
  • Improved: the Restore button on the Backups screen now starts the restore of that backup (you still confirm first).
  • Improved: when a backup finishes, any file that was left out for being over 200 MB is listed.
  • Fixed: the progress bar now always ends at 100% after a successful restore.
  • Fixed: after a restore, a new backup could be refused for a few minutes with “An export is already running”.
  • Removed: the “Free plan: 1 backup stored at a time” note on the Backups screen. It was not accurate.

3.0.3

  • Fixed: the Download button on the Backups page answered “Access denied.” in some browsers. The plugin’s protection against direct URL access to backup files was also catching its own download link; it now checks only the requested path.

3.0.2

  • Fixed: after restoring a backup of a different site, the restored theme and plugin list did not take effect and the previous site kept showing. The restore’s finishing steps could not run once the backup’s users had replaced the current login; they now complete every time.
  • Fixed: a restore could import the database left behind by an earlier, unfinished restore instead of the backup you chose. Every restore now starts clean, and an extracted database is only ever used for the backup it came from.
  • Fixed: the restore no longer overwrites its own plugin files with the copy inside the backup.
  • New: a compatibility check before anything is copied. If a plugin or theme in the backup needs a newer PHP or WordPress than this server has, or there is not enough disk space, the restore stops with a plain explanation and nothing on the site is changed. Smaller differences are shown in the confirmation dialog.
  • New: after the database is restored, plugins that are missing or cannot run on this server are left inactive and listed, and a theme that cannot be used is replaced by a working one, instead of the site failing to load.
  • Security: entries inside a backup can no longer write outside wp-content.
  • Permalinks are regenerated after a restore so the restored site’s URLs work immediately.
  • The security salts in wp-config.php are no longer rewritten after a restore.

3.0.1

  • The optional paid add-on is now called Quick Restore Pro.
  • Removed text from the admin screen that referred to features that are not part of the plugin.
  • Rewrote the plugin description and readme.

3.0

  • The free version now restores backups up to 512 MB. Backups have no limit on total site size. Restoring larger backups requires the optional Quick Restore Pro add-on (one-time purchase, no subscription).
  • Oversized files are refused before upload begins, so no time is wasted uploading a backup that cannot be restored.
  • Added the wpqr_max_restore_size filter so extensions can raise or remove the restore limit.

2.0

  • Critical fix: exports were stuck at “Archiving files… 0 done” forever. The resume position between steps was being written to a discarded copy of the state, so every step restarted from the first file and re-archived the same files endlessly. Fixed by passing state by reference. Exports now resume correctly and complete.
  • Progress counter now updates live during archiving instead of staying frozen.
